newsitem.title: USA: Sun Microsystems reports higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems reports higher profits.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc. Tueday reported a 45 percent jump in first quarter profits, reflecting strong sales of its powerful computer workstations.

The company said profits for the three months ended in September rose to $123.4 million or 63 cents a share, compared with $84.7 million or 42 cents a share in the first quarter of the prior fiscal year. Revenues rose 25 percent to $1.9 billion from $1.5 billion.

The profits were only slightly above the consensus estimate of 61 cents a share, prompting investors to take profits in after-hours trade. Sun, which earlier had jumped $1.625 to $70 a share, tumbled $4 to $66 in after-hours trade.
"These record results can be attributed to our long-time dedication to enterprise network computing," said Scott McNealy, chairman, president and chief executive.

"As the industry increasingly embraces our motto 'The Network Is The Computer,' our market opportunities continue to expand. We are now entering the era of Java computing that features mission-critical servers and thin network clients.

Sun provides workstations, multiprocessing servers, SPARC microprocessors, Solaris operating software and a new programming language called Java for Web-based software that transcends language specific computer operatining systems.
